When the baby is awake and content, lay them tummy-down on your chest. Bring your face level with theirs and talk; smile as they try to lift their head. Start with 1–2 minutes.
Hold the card 20–30 cm from the baby's face. When their gaze fixes, slowly move the card side to side. Stop when they turn their head away.
When the baby makes a sound, softly repeat it and wait. Try to build a back-and-forth “conversation”.
In a warm room, at least 30 minutes after a feed, massage with light, slow strokes starting from the legs. Stop if the baby cries.
While the baby lies on their back, hold the rattle above their chest within reach. When they reach and touch it, celebrate by saying their name.
Lay the baby on their back on the floor and put a favourite toy to one side. As they try to roll, give light support at the hip; don't force the roll.
Tummy time in front of a mirror
During tummy time place the mirror in front of the baby. Watch them engage with their reflection and talk with them.
Copy the baby's sounds like “agu, ba”, then add a new syllable. Wait a few seconds for a reply.
Cover your face with the cloth and uncover it saying “Peekaboo!”. Then give the cloth to the baby and let them pull it off themselves.
Two small toys too big to swallow
Put the toy in one hand, then offer it to the other hand. Encourage using both hands together.
Sit the baby with pillow support and put toys a little to the sides. Watch them keep their balance as they reach; stay right beside them.
Drop a block into the bowl and let them hear the sound. Then give them the block and wait for them to let go.
Wave “bye-bye” when someone leaves the room; clap at the end of a song. Wait for them to copy.
Put the toy at the other end of the sofa. Encourage them to move sideways holding on; pad sharp corners.
Turn the pot upside down and show how to tap it with the wooden spoon. Try fast-slow and loud-quiet beats together.
Put the toys in the box and take them out one by one together. Then turn it into a putting-back game.
Sturdy push cart or empty cardboard box
Accompany the child as they walk pushing the cart. Play on a non-slip floor away from stairs.
Point to a picture and ask “Where is the cat?”. When they show it, repeat the word.
Shape sorter with round and square holes
Start with the round piece. Guide their hand until they find the right hole, then let them try alone.
Tape the paper to the table. Show how to hold the crayon and scribble together; stay close so it doesn't go in the mouth.
Put the ball in front of the child's foot and show how to kick. Hold their hand if needed so they don't fall.
Expand the child's single word into two: when they say “Water”, say “Drink water”. Model, don't correct.
Baby doll, plastic spoon and bowl
Act out feeding the doll and putting it to sleep. Give the child a turn and describe what they're doing.
Mix up the socks and find the pairs together. Say the colour each time you find a pair.
